observation.visible_scene: Close-up of latte-art pouring: a person's right hand cradles a white ceramic cup containing dark espresso with pale crema swirls, while a stainless-steel pitcher held from the upper left tilts and streams white steamed milk into the cup. Background shows a wooden cabinet panel on the left, a dark region top-right, and a mottled light surface bottom-left.
visible_changes: A continuous milk stream flows from the pitcher spout into the cup throughout most of the segment; the stream's landing point stays near the center of the coffee.
The pitcher is gradually lowered toward the cup: the gap between spout and surface shrinks from a long arc in early frames to the spout nearly touching the rim by the late frames.
As the pour continues, the white pattern on the coffee surface shifts and spreads, with the crema swirls reorganizing around the incoming milk.
In the final frames the stream thins to a trickle and then breaks, leaving milk clinging to the spout tip as the pitcher's tilt/height changes.
The cup held in the hand tilts slightly open toward the pitcher over time; the holding hand and thumb on the rim remain in roughly the same position.
The background panel and mottled surface stay largely fixed in frame, indicating the camera is mostly steady while the pitcher and cup move.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the pour began before this excerpt and what final latte-art pattern (if any) is completed after the last frame.
The hand and arm operating the pitcher (only its edge is partly glimpsed at the top-left in later frames).
Whether the pour is finished or paused at the segment's end.
uncertain_details: Whether the apparent slight drift of the cup in frame is camera motion or the holder's hand movement cannot be separated confidently.
The exact moment the milk stream stops is near the boundary of the crop, so completion is not directly confirmed.
